nodes.label: Resume the Claude Code session
nodes.intent: Dig into Claude Code session 9ef739b2-a82f-4d9c-ad69-0d1013ad5066 and let's pick up where it left off
nodes.observed: The work now centers on Mom owning the single correctable map while ingesting the full main and subagent stream without silently missing context. The unresolved design challenge is digesting that stream without doubling model usage or slowing the lead; capture, indexing, retrieval, semantic processing, coverage, lag, and cost must be separated and tested.

nodes.label: Audit pi-tether against the Aaron flow
nodes.intent: Audit it against the Aaron flow from that thread
nodes.observed: The audit established that Tether should adapt Aaron's relationship principles rather than copy its workflow. The current direction is to build the hierarchical lead-and-trail model and its return/landing behavior.

nodes.label: Build the trailing landing and tidy protocol
nodes.intent: go get that
nodes.observed: The implementation direction was revised toward lightweight returns and targeted working-tree checks rather than a mandatory tidy ceremony.

nodes.label: Use safe auto-clean for residue
nodes.intent: Safe auto-clean
nodes.observed: The user selected safe auto-clean: automatically remove only narrowly defined temporary artifacts and report everything else.

nodes.label: Use subagents and delegates
nodes.intent: And it should use subagents/delegates
nodes.observed: The lead required subagents/delegates as part of this direction.

nodes.label: Build the event-driven mother session
nodes.intent: having a almost like a mother thread session sub agent
nodes.observed: The accepted architecture is a slim feed: Mom routinely receives full user messages, existing lead and worker narrative, and lightweight structured tool records, while detailed tool arguments and results remain available for selective source lookup. No summarization model or mandatory reporting turn is added in front of Mom; Mom processes batches and owns the map. The remaining blind spot is facts present only in tool output and never surfaced by an agent, so independent semantic coverage is not claimed.

nodes.label: Have subagents report to the mother thread
nodes.intent: all of our sub agents can report to that thread what it is we're doing, progress we've made, things we're exploring, why we're exploring them
nodes.observed: The user described the mother-thread process as the place where subagents report work, progress, explorations, and reasons for exploration.

nodes.label: Use a separate mother session
nodes.intent: Separate mother
nodes.observed: The user selected a dedicated persistent mother session rather than making the lead the mother.

nodes.label: Wake the mother only for meaningful events
nodes.intent: make it event-driven rather than a continuously thinking model
nodes.observed: The implementation direction is event-driven, with useful check-ins at natural pauses rather than constant progress chatter.

nodes.label: Do not let reminders delete anything
nodes.intent: It should not interrupt work or treat a reminder as permission to delete anything.
nodes.observed: The mother may remind the team to clean the room, but reminders do not authorize deletion.

nodes.label: Do not claim live worker updates without a reporting path
nodes.intent: I won’t present live worker updates as working until there’s an actual reporting path.
nodes.observed: pi-delegate currently reports worker completion, not live progress; a separate mother requires an explicit inter-session reporting channel.

nodes.label: Use an in-process milestone feed
nodes.intent: Recommended: extend pi-delegate with bounded typed activity events and test Tether's receipt without interrupting the lead.
nodes.observed: The user selected the in-process feed option.

nodes.label: Mom maintains all Tether mapping
nodes.intent: Mom does ALL tether
nodes.observed: The user strengthened Postulate #1 into #1b: Mom, rather than Tether or the lead, owns all Tether mapping, history, breadcrumbs, return paths, status answers, and tidy reminders; the Tether UI is only a display and correction surface.

nodes.label: Do not double model usage or slow the lead
nodes.intent: we don't necessarily want to double or more the model usage with this Mom approach, nor do we want to slow things down
nodes.observed: The user set cost and responsiveness as continuing constraints on Mom's architecture; the lead must not be blocked while Mom digests context, and incremental model usage must not be assumed acceptable.

nodes.label: Validate and tune the slim Mom feed
nodes.intent: I’ll prove the smaller feed first: real parent and worker conversations, lightweight tool records, and source lookup—without adding agent reporting calls. Then check whether it preserves enough information for Mom’s map before replacing the live Tether machinery.
nodes.observed: The lead concluded Mom is not ready to replace Tether: the tuned 9/9 result was not independent validation, one citation was lost, and the historical worker session was incomplete. The slim-feed experiment is displaced while the simpler snapshot approach is tested.

nodes.label: Reconcile superseded records in the same patch
nodes.intent: when Mom records a changed decision or reported completion, reconcile the older record in the same patch while preserving unaffected facts
nodes.observed: GPT-6 Astra recommended this narrower fix after confirming that the three stale-record failures were visible in the feed; the lead labeled those transitions and is adding negative controls before testing it.

nodes.label: Test replacement snapshots for Mom
nodes.intent: I’ll test replacement snapshots on the same feed and model.
nodes.observed: The fixed comparison and authority-boundary tests completed successfully, but the experiment is complete and has been explicitly displaced by bounded live integration rather than another representation redesign.

nodes.label: Keep the snapshot comparison fixed
nodes.intent: One fixed comparison. No keyword selector, aging rules, or tuning against the results.
nodes.observed: The fixed comparison governed the completed snapshot experiment and remains historical to that parked work.

nodes.label: Retain continuing decisions through rewrites
nodes.intent: I’ll focus on the two failures: keeping older decisions through rewrites, and staying quiet when nothing is being overlooked.
nodes.observed: The next test keeps exact raw user instructions beside the rewritten page so continuing decisions remain available through final snapshots.

nodes.label: Advise only on overlooked obligations
nodes.intent: For advice, Mom must point to an existing obligation and new evidence that it’s being overlooked—not merely say work is unfinished.
nodes.observed: The lead defined a source-backed advice condition: an existing obligation plus new evidence of oversight, rather than unfinished work alone.

nodes.label: Label only actors in the current batch
nodes.intent: label only this batch’s actors
nodes.observed: The lead identified historical worker-roster entries being misread as newly pending and adopted current-batch actor labeling as the bounded correction.

nodes.label: Pair failure consults with matched tool evidence
nodes.intent: give explicit failure consults the matched tool invocation plus result within the existing two-page budget
nodes.observed: The lead adopted matched invocation-and-result evidence after a historical error answer guessed without inspecting the caller.

nodes.label: Drive the live Mom integration in tmux
nodes.intent: I’ll drive the implementation and live checks.
nodes.observed: The next implementation is a single live cutover inside pi-tether, driven in a separate tmux Pi session. The current batch shows automatic observation, atomic checkpoints, cached status, and no ledger-writing tool type-checking; recovery, live worker capture, and the isolated Pi session are now being exercised. The scope remains bounded to the current session and pi-delegate workers, with no additional watcher model or representation redesign.

nodes.label: Keep live integration bounded to this session
nodes.intent: Scope: current session—including reopening it—and `pi-delegate` workers.
nodes.observed: The live implementation scope excludes cross-session merging, lesson routing, and a broader harness rewrite.

nodes.label: Verify live behavior in the isolated Pi session
nodes.intent: I’ll implement the cutover here, then exercise reload, worker returns, recovery, and quiet notices there.
nodes.observed: The lead is using a separate tmux dogfood Pi instance to exercise the cutover while leaving the main session alone.
